assumedContext: No primary filing could be retrieved: every external domain is blocked by this environment's egress proxy. Findings rest on search-result summaries of the FY2025 results release, the June 2026 share capital increase documentation and Greek and Cypriot press.

STRUCTURE. ADMIE Holding is a holding company whose sole asset is a 51% stake in IPTO S.A., the Greek transmission system operator. The remaining 49% is held by the Greek state (through DES ADMIE) and State Grid Corporation of China. Every figure in this dossier is therefore a look-through of IPTO at 51%, and that is stated wherever it applies.

A widely syndicated headline reported the June 2026 share issue price as EUR 1.00. That figure is the nominal-value context, not the offer. The offer was 130,864,197 new shares at EUR 4.17, completed 18 June 2026. The EUR 1.00 figure is not used anywhere in this dossier.

findings.claim: This is the only genuinely regulated business in the batch, and the thesis's framing fits it in a way it did not fit PPC. IPTO is the Greek electricity transmission system operator: a legal monopoly, remunerated on a regulated asset base, with revenue set by the regulator rather than by a market.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Pricing power is therefore neither commercial nor competitive — it is the allowed return. The company cannot raise price, cannot lose share and cannot be disintermediated. What it can suffer is a regulatory reset, and that is the entire risk architecture of the equity.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: The growth mechanism in the thesis is real, funded and specific. IPTO's 2026-2029 Strategic Plan carries roughly EUR 6bn of investment and is intended to take the regulated asset base from about EUR 3.3bn in 2025 to roughly EUR 7bn by 2029 — very nearly a doubling.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE
findings.source: IPTO 2026-2029 Strategic Plan and capital increase documentation
findings.unit: EUR bn regulated asset base target 2029

findings.claim: That is the cleanest growth mechanism in this batch. A regulated network earns its allowed return on whatever it is permitted to invest, so RAB growth converts almost mechanically into earnings growth — with no volume risk, no price risk and no counterparty risk.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: But shareholders funded it, and the thesis does not say so. ADMIE Holding issued 130,864,197 new shares at EUR 4.17 in a non-preemptive book-build completed on 18 June 2026, raising roughly EUR 530-546m to fund its 51% pro-rata participation in IPTO's EUR 1bn capital increase. Against 232m shares previously outstanding that is a 56% increase in the share count.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: The issue was non-preemptive, so existing holders received no rights and no compensating instrument. The dilution was uncompensated, though the EUR 4.17 price was only a modest discount to the market — a materially healthier structure than a deeply discounted rights issue.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: This is the second Greek company in this batch to fund a grid build by materially diluting shareholders in 2026. PPC increased its share count by 62% in April; ADMIE Holding by 56% in June. Both descriptions in the thesis set present the plan and omit who paid for it.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived; cross-reference to the PPC dossier in this batch

findings.claim: Profitability moved the wrong way in the most recent reported year. Consolidated adjusted net profit was EUR 132.4m in FY2025 against EUR 157.9m in FY2024, a decline of about 16%, in a business whose asset base was growing.
findings.label: FACT
findings.unit: EUR m FY2025 adjusted net profit

gaps.item: The current regulatory period's allowed WACC and its reset date
gaps.whyItMatters: For a regulated network the allowed return IS the pricing power. A 50bp change moves earnings and fair value materially, and the reset timetable is the principal event risk.

gaps.item: The cause of the 16% FY2025 profit decline
gaps.whyItMatters: A regulated network with a growing asset base should not normally see profit fall. Whether this is interest cost, depreciation phasing or a regulatory adjustment changes the forward picture entirely.

gaps.item: IPTO net debt and gearing against the RAB
gaps.whyItMatters: Every look-through valuation in Phase 5 depends on it, and it is the input this dossier is least sure of.

gaps.item: Whether ADMIE Holding equity-accounts or consolidates IPTO
gaps.whyItMatters: Determines whether the reported EUR 132.4m is the group figure or the holding company's share, which changes per-share earnings by roughly a factor of two.

risks.text: The share count rose 56% in June 2026 through a non-preemptive issue, so existing holders were diluted without rights and the thesis does not mention it.
The allowed return is set by the regulator and is the entire pricing-power architecture. A WACC reset is the principal event risk and its timing is not established here.
FY2025 adjusted net profit fell about 16% to EUR 132.4m in a year when the asset base was growing, and the cause is not established.
The listed vehicle owns 51% of the operating company, so it controls neither the dividend policy nor the capital plan outright.

catalysts.text: FY2026 results — the first full picture on the enlarged share count
Regulatory decision on the allowed WACC for the next period
RAB progression disclosure toward the EUR 7bn 2029 target

conclusions: This is the only genuinely regulated business in the batch, and the thesis's framing fits it where it did not fit PPC. IPTO is a legal monopoly remunerated on a regulated asset base — no volume risk, no price risk, no counterparty risk.

The growth mechanism is the cleanest here: roughly EUR 6bn of investment taking the regulated asset base from about EUR 3.3bn in 2025 to roughly EUR 7bn by 2029. In a regulated network, RAB growth converts almost mechanically into earnings growth.

But shareholders funded it. ADMIE Holding issued 130,864,197 shares at EUR 4.17 in a non-preemptive book-build in June 2026 — a 56% increase in the share count — to fund its 51% share of IPTO's EUR 1bn capital increase. The thesis does not mention it.

That makes two Greek companies in this batch that funded a grid build by materially diluting shareholders in 2026: PPC by 62% in April, ADMIE Holding by 56% in June. Both descriptions present the plan and omit who paid for it.

And profit moved the wrong way in the last reported year: adjusted net profit fell about 16% to EUR 132.4m from EUR 157.9m, in a business whose asset base was growing. The cause is not established here and it is the most important thing this dossier does not know.
thesisImpact: Phase 1 confirms the regulated architecture and the RAB mechanism, and establishes that the share count has risen 56%. Phase 5 must value the company per share on the enlarged base and must test whether the 'yield' half of the thesis survives a build funded partly by shareholders.
